parts.note: Bugs is read as the cartoon rabbit's first name, so the clue asks for the pet animal that completes his famous name

explanation.surface: An exasperated owner says this pet is driving them mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' looks like a verb meaning annoys, but it is the first name of the Warner Bros cartoon rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit kept as a pet is fondly called by this childish name, which also completes the cartoon character's name.

parts.note: Hood is Little Red Riding Hood, and her adversary is the villain of the fairy tale who eats her grandmother

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' suggests a gangster or Robin Hood; it is Little Red Riding Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale villain who menaces Little Red Riding Hood is the wicked wolf of the story.

clue.text: Need a tip about the low water

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the preceding words are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone needs advice about when the water will be low.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide with the smallest range, coming twice a month, gives the lowest high water.

indicators.note: became signals that the letters of Old Leery are changed into another form

explanation.surface: An old man called Leery took up singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sings in the warbling Alpine style is a kind of singer.

clue.text: Chief of the Air Staff met with an acceptable confederate accidentally

parts.note: CAS is the abbreviation for Chief of the Air Staff, the head of the RAF
U means upper-class and hence socially acceptable
a confederate is an ally

explanation.surface: The head of the RAF happened by chance to meet a suitable partner.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, hence acceptable, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something casually means doing it by chance, without design, so the adverbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Yield to tennis ace, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud and replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a top tennis player is ranked as a seed in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: A player gives way to a tennis star, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says SEED aloud, which gives the soundalike CEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up territory or a point is to yield it, so the verbs are synonyms.

definitions.meaning: joins means brings together into one
confederates as a verb means forms an alliance, brings together

explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean bring or come together as one, the second as a verb rather than the noun.

parts.note: read as freed from punishment out of mercy, while discharged also hints at firing a gun or a firework

explanation.definitionFit: Someone excused punishment is released leniently, and a firework or gun is fired, both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Get the measure of the police

definitions.meaning: a unit of length of three feet
the ... is short for Scotland ..., headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Someone tries to size up the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, often just called the Yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of measure of three feet; and Scotland Yard, standing for the London police force.

parts.note: grand means imposing or showy
dad is a parent

explanation.surface: A family member is described as a flamboyant father.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a family relative, called by this informal name.

clue.text: Actor goes in a certain direction to the forest

parts.note: east is one of the compass directions
a wood is a forest

explanation.surface: A performer heads off one way into the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Clint of that surname is a famous American film actor, so the name is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Took off cloak in disgusted condition

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective: being in a disgusted state

indicators.note: in signals that one piece sits inside another

parts.note: took off means imitated or mimicked, aped
a pall is a cloak or covering

explanation.surface: Someone removed their cape, feeling sickened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' looks like removing clothes but means mimicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being horrified and revolted is being in a disgusted state of mind.

parts.note: anti means against
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A certain figure opposes the official record.
explanation.definitionFit: An antilogarithm is the specific number whose logarithm is given.

clue.text: Good tackle for fishing for eels

parts.note: rigging is tackle, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Decent gear is needed when angling for eels.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigs are small eels, and catching them is a specialist word for fishing for eels.

parts.note: repose is rest or sleep

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: Restful sleep seems entire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' gives FUL, the spelling heard in FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restful and tranquil is calm, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Lethargically having no schedule to empty lorry

parts.note: a schedule is a list, so having no list is jokingly list-less

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word lorry is removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A driver idles with no timetable, about to unload the lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without energy or enthusiasm is acting lethargically, so the adverbs are synonyms.

indicators.note: however suggests things may be done in any way at all, so the letters of the fodder may be arranged however

explanation.surface: A tidy middle-class person nevertheless does as told.
explanation.definitionFit: Following orders means complying with the rules laid down, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Brown men just meet and touch

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing nouns: lines that just meet a curve and touch it

parts.note: tan is a brown colour
gents are men

explanation.surface: Suntanned men barely meet and make contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just meet and touch' describes the geometry lines rather than an action.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry such straight lines touch a curve at one point without crossing it.

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to posit is to place or put forward

explanation.surface: An office faces east.
explanation.definitionFit: Being across from something is facing it, so the words are synonyms.

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone greets Frances and asks her to amend the charter.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a right or licence granted by charter, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: A first-class lag crazy about Grace

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of lag are jumbled
about signals that the following piece is turned round

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: A top convict goes mad over a woman called Grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' turns LAG into GLA; 'about' turns AI into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglaia is one of the three Graces of Greek myth, an example of the definition.

indicators.note: in signals the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Patients are listed by name in the doctor's account book.
explanation.definitionFit: Named and called both mean given a name, so the participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Track the burrow to a dreadful abode

parts.note: to dog is to follow or track
a hole is a burrow

explanation.surface: Someone follows an animal to its lair, a nasty home.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-hole is a squalid, wretched place to live, an idiom for a dreadful dwelling.

clue.text: Study of wood by 3 unknown characters about to behold a plank

indicators.note: about signals that one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: in algebra x and y are unknowns, here x and y and y again
lo is an old word meaning behold
a log is a piece of timber, like a plank

explanation.surface: A researcher examines timber with three mystery letters around a board.
explanation.walkthrough: X and Y are the usual algebraic unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -logy means study and xylo- means wood, so this is the science of wood.

clue.text: Short celebration for those with ten degrees

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
MAs are degrees, Masters of Arts

explanation.surface: A brief party is held for graduates with ten qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of the name of the Christmas festival, a celebration.

indicators.note: 50:50 means half and half, so each name gives its second half

explanation.surface: Kaye and Leah split everything evenly and agree.
explanation.walkthrough: '50:50' takes the second half of Kaye and of Leah.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word of assent, a casual synonym.

indicators.note: fashionable suggests the letters of nieces are styled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some necessities, such as stylish nieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigencies are pressing requirements, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Careless work of hit and run merchant

parts.note: slap means hit
dash means run

explanation.surface: Shoddy work by a hit-and-run driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is hasty and careless, so the adjectives are synonyms.

parts.note: to view is to see

indicators.note: hollowed-out removes the inside of dinghy, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A grubby scene glimpsed from an empty little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Grotty is British slang for shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means shabby and squalid, synonyms for the slang word.
